clauses: allow_nan=false raises ValueError for NaN or infinity instead of emitting nonstandard values.

sources.label: json.dumps documentation
sources.text: If allow_nan is false (default: True), then it will be a ValueError to serialize out of range float values (nan, inf, -inf) in strict compliance of the JSON specification. If allow_nan is true, their JavaScript equivalents (NaN, Infinity, -Infinity) will be used.

controls.answer: According to the documentation: If allow_nan is false (default: True), then it will be a ValueError to serialize out of range float values (nan, inf, -inf) in strict compliance of the JSON specification. If allow_nan is true, their JavaScript equivalents (NaN, Infinity, -Infinity) will be used.
Passing allow_nan=False makes the encoder raise a ValueError when it meets NaN or an infinity, rather than writing NaN or Infinity tokens that strict JSON does not allow.
allow_nan=false emits NaN as the JavaScript token, so nothing is raised.
With allow_nan=False the encoder silently replaces NaN and the infinities with null.
